stem: Why is a flawless demo weak evidence an LLM feature works?
options: It is one sample from a non-deterministic system on one input you happened to try
explanation: Output is sampled (2.7), the input is not representative, and fluency is not correctness (2.8).

options: A pass rate over a representative, labelled set, measured the same way every time
A second opinion from the model
explanation: 3.3's held-out set and metrics, applied to a language-output component.

options: Gates a change against a golden set before it ships
explanation: Fast, cheap, per-PR; catches known regressions.

options: Watches production and reveals cases the golden set did not contain
explanation: Complement, not alternative; every miss becomes an offline case.

stem: A team with only offline evals…
options: Ships confidently into surprises the set never contained
explanation: Offline cannot contain what it has never seen; online is the watch.

stem: The eval loop is closed by…
options: Every production miss and incident becoming a new golden-set case
explanation: The set is the memory that stops the same bug shipping twice.

stem: The unit of an eval measurement is…
options: A rate over several runs, not a single pass
explanation: One run of a sampled system measures luck (2.7).

options: Read a sample of the failures - the rate says something moved, the sample says what

stem: New prompt 84%, old 82%, set run once. Is it better?
options: Not yet - run several times and check no slice/case regressed; 2 points may be noise

stem: A prompt change is done when…
options: It looks good in a demo
A number says it did not make things worse, on a representative set, past a pre-set threshold
explanation: Treat a prompt change as a deploy gated on a measurement.
